name: Surveyor 2 to 7
short_status: Six-mission conclusion of the US Surveyor program, Sep 1966 to Feb 1968: four soft-landed (Surveyors 3, 5, 6, 7), two failed (2 crashed, 4 vanished). Apollo 12 later visited Surveyor 3, the only robotic craft humans have ever returned to.
tagline: NASA and JPL · United States · Lander · 1966 · The space race Partial
stats: robotic craft humans have ever returned to (Surveyor 3, by Apollo 12)
first liftoff from another world (Surveyor 6's hop, 17 Nov 1967)
returned by the four successful landers (3, 5, 6, 7)

facts.label: Program scope
facts.value: Surveyors 2 to 7 flew from 20 Sep 1966 to 7 Jan 1968; four landed successfully (3, 5, 6, 7) and two failed (2 crashed, 4 lost on descent)

facts.label: Builder and launch vehicle
facts.value: Spacecraft built by Hughes Aircraft, managed by NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory, launched on Atlas-Centaur from Cape Canaveral

facts.label: Surveyor 2 failure
facts.value: Launched 20 Sep 1966; one of three vernier thrusters failed to ignite for a midcourse correction on Sep 21, throwing the craft into a spin (39 attempts to fire it failed); it crashed 23 Sep 1966 southeast of Copernicus near 5.5 N, 12 W

facts.label: Surveyor 3 landing
facts.value: Launched 17 Apr 1967; landed 20 Apr 1967 at 00:04 UT in southeastern Oceanus Procellarum; reflective rocks confused its descent radar and the vernier engines failed to cut off, so it bounced twice before settling

facts.label: Surveyor 3 site (LROC)
facts.value: LROC mean-observed position 3.0162 S, 336.5820 E; Apollo 12's LM sat at 3.0128 S, 336.5781 E, about 155 to 157 m away

facts.label: Apollo 12 visit to Surveyor 3
facts.value: On 19 to 20 Nov 1969, Pete Conrad and Alan Bean walked to Surveyor 3 and cut off its television camera, scoop and cabling to return to Earth after 31 months on the Moon; the camera is now in the Smithsonian National Air and Space Museum

facts.label: Surveyor 4 failure
facts.value: Launched 14 Jul 1967 toward Sinus Medii; radio contact cut out two seconds before retro-rocket cutoff on Jul 17, about two and a half minutes before touchdown, with the retrorocket suspected to have exploded; no wreck has been identified

facts.label: Surveyor 5 rescue and first soil chemistry
facts.value: Launched 8 Sep 1967; controllers nursed it through a near-fatal helium-regulator leak to land Sep 11 in Mare Tranquillitatis, where its alpha-scattering instrument made the first chemical analysis of soil on another world (basaltic, more than half oxygen by atom)

facts.label: Surveyor 6 hop
facts.value: Landed Sinus Medii 10 Nov 1967; on 17 Nov 1967 it fired its vernier engines for 2.5 seconds, rose about 10 ft and set down some 8 ft to the west, the first liftoff from another celestial body

facts.label: Surveyor 7 at Tycho
facts.value: Launched 7 Jan 1968; landed 10 Jan 1968 on the ejecta blanket north of Tycho at 40.97 S, 11.44 W, the only Surveyor to reach the lunar highlands; ran a camera, alpha-scattering analyzer (three samples) and soil-mechanics scoop

facts.label: Surveyor 7 laser detection
facts.value: On 20 Jan 1968 its camera detected two argon lasers aimed at it from Kitt Peak National Observatory, Arizona and Table Mountain, Wrightwood, California, an early pointing and optical-communication test; contact was lost 21 Feb 1968, ending the program

facts.label: Images returned by the four successful landers
facts.value: Surveyor 3 returned 6,326; Surveyor 5 about 20,018; Surveyor 6 about 29,952; Surveyor 7 about 21,274 (over 77,000 combined), feeding Apollo site selection and lander design

timeline: Surveyor 2 launches from Cape Canaveral toward Sinus Medii
Surveyor 2 crashes southeast of Copernicus after a thruster failed to fire and the craft tumbled
Surveyor 3 lands in Oceanus Procellarum, bouncing twice when its engines failed to cut off
Surveyor 4 signal is lost about two and a half minutes before touchdown, retrorocket suspected to have exploded
Surveyor 5 lands in Mare Tranquillitatis after a helium-leak descent; its alpha-scattering instrument makes the first chemical analysis of soil on another world
Surveyor 6 fires its verniers and hops about 10 ft, the first liftoff from another celestial body
Surveyor 7 lands on the Tycho ejecta blanket, the only Surveyor to reach the highlands
Surveyor 7 detects two argon lasers aimed at it from Earth observatories
Final contact with Surveyor 7 ends the Surveyor program
Apollo 12 lands beside Surveyor 3; the crew later cuts off and returns its camera, the only human revisit to a robotic craft on another world
